title: Canonical BHV-####.md, hydrated representation
description: The one canonical shape a behavior document must validate against, regardless of which step (b4, c1, c2) last wrote to it. This validates the HYDRATED representation of a BHV-####.md — the YAML frontmatter block merged with the parsed '## Scenarios' table (-> scenarios) and '## Decision tables' section (-> decision_tables), assembled by whatever parses the .md file, not the raw frontmatter block in isolation. 'scenarios' and 'decision_tables' are required content this schema validates, but they live in Markdown body sections, not the YAML frontmatter, in the .md file itself — see templates/BHV-template.md's header comment.

risk_tier.description: Assigned mechanically by b5 (docs/phase-b-behaviors.md, 'Risk tier'); gates how Phase C's c5 branch-triage gate applies. Not the same gate as Phase B's inventory-coverage completeness check, which is not risk-tiered.

high_risk_override.description: Human-set. True forces risk_tier: full regardless of taxonomy — for a behavior that touches money, authorization, or a state transition but whose taxonomy wouldn't otherwise trigger full triage.

bpmn_source_engine.description: Only present when taxonomy == process; copied verbatim from framework.yaml. Renamed from bpmn_target: the framework records which engine's execution semantics the carried-over .bpmn files assume, and has no opinion on the target engine. See DECISIONS.md, 'BPMN definitions are shipped as discovered'.

neighborhood_diagram.description: Mermaid source for this behavior's capped 2-hop neighborhood, generated deterministically alongside b3 from the same neighborhood_nodes/neighborhood_edges — never hand-edited, never LLM-authored. See docs/phase-b-behaviors.md, 'Neighborhood diagram.'

legacy_refs.description: Aggregated file:line spans across every covered node.

covers.description: Inventory node IDs this behavior claims via COVERS edges.

origin.description: legacy: derived from evidence, and the replacement is expected to reproduce it. new: a deliberate addition with no legacy precedent, human-authored. legacy-defect: true of the legacy system and known to be wrong — still evidenced, still rendered, still run against the legacy app by c4, but carrying a disposition so it does not reach an implementer as an ordinary requirement.

disposition.description: Required when origin is legacy-defect, null otherwise. preserve: the replacement keeps the behavior. fix: the replacement deliberately does not reproduce it, and replaced_by_scenario_id names what it does instead.

replaced_by_scenario_id.description: Required when disposition is fix: the origin: new scenario stating the replacement's behavior. Without it, 'fix' says what not to build and nothing about what to build.

decision_table_ref.description: Non-null means this row is a plain-language summary of one row of the referenced decision_tables entry, and is NOT independently rendered — see templates/renderers/*.md.

decision_tables.description: Decision tables are canonical content c3 renders and c6 validates, but were previously unrepresentable under additionalProperties: false. Parsed from the '## Decision tables' section of the .md file, one entry per DT-BHV-####-NN table.

backs_scenario.description: The scenario_id whose decision_table_ref points here.

reduced_by.description: framework.yaml: combinatorial_reducer, if this table (or a sub-table layered on it) went through c2b's pairwise reduction. null for MC/DC rows, which are never pairwise-reduced.

values.description: Maps each entry in sub_conditions to that row's value for it.
